newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Continental unit launches superferry.
newsitem.headline: Irish Continental unit launches superferry.

text.p: Irish Continental's subsidiary Irish Ferries was due to launch a new 60-million-Irish-pound superferry in Rotterdam on Friday.
The superferry, with a capacity of up to 2,300 passengers and crew, will go into service between Dublin and Holyhead in Wales in February 1997, Irish Ferries said.
The launch of the 33,000-tonne Isle of Inishmore ferry represents a total investment of over 180 million Irish pounds by Irish Ferries in vessels and shore facilities since 1992.

In welcoming the launch of the Isle of Inismore, Irish minister of state Eamon Gilmore said the Irish government had introduced fiscal incentives for leasing more efficient and environmentally friendly vessels for use on Irish sea routes.
Meanwhile, 200 Irish Ferries staff said on Thursday they would march on the Irish parliament next week over proposed company plans to lay them off for seven months.
Irish Ferries announced in September it was ending its winter continental passenger services to France and that this may result in company redundancies.
